notVerifiable.reason: vLLM allocates KV memory as tokens are written and BLIS translates vLLM, so neither has a policy that reserves a whole prompt before admitting it; there is no counterpart to compare.
vLLM does not reserve KV memory for a request's whole output at admission, and BLIS follows vLLM, so there is no counterpart to compare.
vLLM does no static batching (it schedules continuously) and BLIS translates vLLM, so there is no counterpart to compare.

BLIS reloads whenever its host-memory tier holds the prefix; it has no decision between copying and recomputing to compare. The scenario that exercises the tier (tiers-offload) is a check of the tiers, not of this rule.

BLIS replays traces and generates open-loop streams; it has no counterpart to the closed-loop sessions (users who wait, think and return) that the site generates, so the scenarios feed both simulators a trace instead.

It is how both simulators are given the same requests, not a mechanism BLIS models: every scenario uses it, and the conformance machinery fails when the two row sets differ, but there is nothing in BLIS to compare it with.
